name: How close can an outdoor living structure be to the property line?

mainEntity.name: What setback rules apply to patio covers, pergolas, and outdoor kitchens near property lines?
mainEntity.text: What setback rules apply to patio covers, pergolas, and outdoor kitchens near property lines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setbacks are one of the most common reasons outdoor living projects get delayed. A patio cover, pergola, barbecue enclosure, or accessory structure placed too close to a property line may require redesign or zoning review. The required distance can depend on the city, the height and type of structure, fire-rating concerns, easements, and whether the project is attached to the home. In dense neighborhoods like Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, lot constraints often make setbacks the first issue to check. A good preconstruction review should confirm lot lines, utility easements, and any special district rules before plans are finalized. That prevents expensive changes after plans are already drawn.
acceptedAnswer.description: Setback rules vary by city and project type, but property-line clearance is a major permit issue in Los Angeles-area outdoor construction. Structures near lot lines often require zoning review before construction.
